solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He might buy copper's big book, dear in end

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper, with the S of the possessive kept
a tome is a large, heavy volume

indicators.note: in end asks for only the final letter of the word dear

explanation.surface: A shopper is described through a policeman's hefty volume and an expensive closing price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper is someone who might buy, so the definition describes a client by what they do.

clue.text: Conservative girl in charge — top quality!

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the UK political party
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: A Tory young woman runs things with excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic is of the highest, most enduring standard.

clue.text: Reduced pace in Oslo monastery

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words Oslo monastery

explanation.surface: Life moves slowly in a Norwegian religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: Slo-mo is short for slow motion, playback at a reduced speed.

clue.text: Event Hello! arranged? True

indicators.note: arranged asks whether the letters of event hello are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity magazine's staged event is questioned as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity gossip magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the level is an idiom for honest or genuine.

clue.text: Substitute some tigers at zoo

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some captive big cats stand in for wild ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing, so a stand-in.

clue.text: Pig having short time inside pack

indicators.note: inside, after having, means the pig word holds the time letter within itself

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A farm animal seems to hold a brief moment within as it gets packed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: By comparison, small adolescent, say? That is right

parts.note: a teen is an example of an adolescent
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A youngster is described as rather small, and correctly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenier is the comparative of teeny, tiny, so it means smaller than something else.

clue.text: Charlie — old Berlin feature? Primarily yes

parts.note: the Berlin Wall divided the city until 1989

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word yes

explanation.surface: A tourist named Charlie is asked about a feature of old Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie and wally are both British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a silly person, just like a wally.

clue.text: A job so ungodly ultimately leading to giving up religion

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
so and as can both mean 'in the way that'

indicators.note: ultimately asks for only the last letter of the word ungodly

explanation.surface: An impious line of work seems to lead someone to abandon their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the renunciation of a faith, exactly the abandoning of religious belief.

clue.text: Enthusiasm of Zoe, early regularly

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of Zoe early, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Zoe shows keenness by turning up ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal is eager fervour, a direct synonym for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Retiree, pro, recollected standard works

indicators.note: read as re-collected, the letters of retiree pro are gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: A retired professional remembers their classic pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertoire is the stock of pieces a performer or company regularly plays.

clue.text: Ignoring resistance, made great effort to provide heater

indicators.note: ignoring means the resistance letter is left out of the effort word

parts.note: strove is the past tense of strive, to try hard
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone battles hard, unopposed, to get a heater for the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A stove is an appliance that burns fuel to warm a room, so it is a kind of heater.

clue.text: Tetchy, I abandoned financial centre

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of Tetchy I run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: An irritable person quits the world of banking.
explanation.definitionFit: The City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and markets, Britain's financial centre.

clue.text: Long to be in environment of court prestige

indicators.note: the longing word sits within the surroundings formed by the court letters

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to move in courtly circles for the status it brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is the distinction or kudos something carries, a synonym of prestige.

clue.text: More annoyed seeing burden on monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the burden word sits above the monarch letters

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler grows irritated by a heavy load placed upon them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosser is the comparative of cross, angry, so it means angrier.

clue.text: Scarcity of daughters where we live?

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies
our planet Earth is where all of us live

explanation.surface: A question wonders whether the world lacks daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a shortage or lack, the same as a scarcity.

clue.text: In speech greeting girl's method of promoting cleanliness

indicators.note: in speech means the greeting is heard rather than read

parts.note: saying 'Hi, Jean!' is greeting a girl named Jean

explanation.surface: Someone talks of saying hello to a girl as a way of keeping clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the practice of keeping oneself and surroundings clean to protect health.

clue.text: Acceptable to house the Spanish cat

indicators.note: the acceptable word holds the Spanish article inside it

parts.note: fine means satisfactory or acceptable
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: It is fine to keep a Spanish cat at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline is a noun for any member of the cat family.

clue.text: In favour of note for example backing person aided by patronage

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: backing means the letters of the example abbreviation are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A supporter writes a reference note to back a promising newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone helped and promoted by an influential patron or mentor.

clue.text: Extremely prickly academic put out by London steel structure

indicators.note: extremely asks for the two end letters of the word prickly
put out by means the academic is ejected from the word London

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A touchy lecturer is upset by London's steel landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice tower carrying power lines.

clue.text: Not half unearthing obsession?

indicators.note: not half means dropping the front half of unearthing, keeping only its second five letters

explanation.surface: Someone digs things up with a mania that is more than half-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an idiom for a fixation, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Counting everyone home — a long list, just starting

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: just starting asks for the opening letter of each of long and list

explanation.surface: A roll call at home starts on a lengthy list of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means altogether, as a total including every person.

clue.text: Very rich, he drinks too much

definitions.meaning: ... vegetation or decor is luxuriant and opulent
slang for a heavy drinker or alcoholic

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is portrayed as a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is luxuriant or opulent; the other is a slang noun for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Initially losing it, then irritated, spectators take legal action

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of losing, it, then and irritated

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators paying to attend a sports match

explanation.surface: Angry onlookers lose their temper and decide to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' governs four words, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to go to law, bringing a lawsuit against someone.

clue.text: Never an artist, this girl?

parts.note: no can mean not ever, as in 'no way'
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for an artist

explanation.surface: A woman is asked whether she has never been a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a female forename, so the question mark flags a girl given by example.

clue.text: Terribly vile leer — wake-up call

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of vile leer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful lecherous look serves as an unwelcome alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal sounded to rouse soldiers in the morning.
